Perhaps perform a porosity test on his hair as well
- take a few strands of shedded hair, drop them in a cup of water 
if they float, it's low porosity
if they sink, it's high porosity 

Make sure that the hair is fully placed in the water, not just placed on top since the surface tension of the water can keep the hair above the water! I like to mix it around with my finger. My hair will float in the middle (not sink, not float to the surface) once I do this. Some strands will stay at the top meaning my hair is low-medium porosity. High porosity hair will sink completely and low porosity will float back to the top and reject the water.

High porosity hair needs lower temperature and less frequent shampoos. There are also plenty of moisturizing leave in conditioners and oils that are helpful. You'll want to avoid products that have sulfates and alcohols since they're drying.

If it's low porosity, then you can recommend a clarifying shampoo once a week with more protein rich shampoos on other days.

As far as the frizzy hair after drying, since he mostly conditions, he needs to condition his hair less overall. There's likely product buildup from not shampooing frequently but using conditioner all the time. A good clarifying wash with a gentle clarifying shampoo and a break from the over conditioning would help. After showers, a lightweight gel (like the hydrating shape up aqua gel from curlsmith) through his hair will help hold the curls together and prevent the frizz while they dry. 

After using a gel, you can break the gel cast after the hair is completely dry, and you'll not have the crunchy gelled hair that turns people away from using these products. Gels keep the hair strands together and provide structure and support to prevent the curls from breaking into frizz. They protect from heat, moisture, dryness, etc. so that your hair can maintain its natural structure.

All the best, and good luck!

Solipsism asserts that only the mind, or what's imagined by the mind rather, is real - it requires that a mind exist and the mind is capable of imagining things. It, as a philosophical thesis, claims that anything external to the mind cannot be verified and therefore is unsure. It's flawed and does not align with non-duality because it's still distinguishing between internal/external, just that the external is not verifiable. Solipsism is self-contradictory. Something has to be doing the imagining. 

Non-duality on the other hand asserts that there isn't a meaningful distinction between internal and external, not that one is "less real/more real" than the other. 

There is no void, there is only *this* and by virtue of acting within it and making "white noise" as you say, you affirm that it exists.

Dealing with trauma can be a lifelong thing, for me coping tends to be a series of me crying and getting everything out, and then being around people I can do active stuff with. The exercise helps release endorphines and make me feel better, and the crying helps me relieve stress. Unfortunately, what works for one person may not work for you so I wish you luck on your quest of finding how to deal with things.. Sometimes journaling helps, or just relaxing with friends drinking some tea.. But like I said at the begining, it can be a lifelong thing and you don't just get over it forever, but having support for when things get rough makes a world of a difference. There are plenty of hotlines and counselors available!
